params.body:
## What

The monitor (the Observatory wall, and the status the MCP tool reads) now judges the deploy, from the files `bin/auto-deploy` already leaves on the box:

- **A merge is not going out** (`nu`): a commit the tests on the box turned down (`~/.auto-deploy/<dir>.rejected`). The evidence names the repo, the refused commit, how long it has been held back, the failing tests from `/tmp/tw-deploy-tests.log`, and the commit the box stays on.
- **Auto-deploy is failing** (`deze week`): the last round ended `failed` without a refused commit (a fetch or a build).
- **Auto-deploy has stopped running** (`deze week`): the status file is older than 30 minutes, while the cron runs every 2.
- A machine without auto-deploy state is a blind spot named Deploy, never an all-clear.

`measure()` takes the reading itself (`measureDeploy()`, overridable for tests), so the test that checks every judged measurement is produced covers it too.

## Why

On 2026-10-10 one test read the live model settings and failed every round. The box stayed on #311 for hours while #312, #313 and #314 waited, merged and not live. The script wrote its refusal into a state file and a log, and the wall, the Observatory status and the monitor all stayed calm. It came out only because someone ran a script that was not on the box yet.

Severity `nu`: a refused api commit also holds back the frontends of the same round, so nothing merged goes live until a person fixes main.

## Tests

`test/monitor.test.mjs`: three new cases (reading a refused commit with its failing tests and the finding it makes; a failed round and a silent cron; no state is a blind spot). The healthy fixture carries a deploy reading. Full suite: 1162 pass, 6 fail. The 6 are the report-render tests, which need `pdftoppm`; the workbench lacks it and the box has it.
params.title: The wall says when a merge is not going out
